subject.title: Group chat context handling can blur which messages are addressed to the current agent

question: What permanent target-state contract should OpenClaw expose for multi-agent group history and Telegram reply chains?
rationale: Current source proves the missing metadata, but deciding sibling-bot identity discovery, unknown versus ambient semantics, and whether this belongs in core channel contracts requires maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Define Core Target Metadata
options.body: Approve a narrow core/channel contract for per-message current-agent, other-agent, and ambient target facts, then implement Telegram first with tests and live proof.

options.title: Prompt-Only Mitigation
options.body: Treat PR 78054-style wording as an interim mitigation and defer durable metadata until a later design pass.

options.title: Leave To Plugins
options.body: Decline core metadata for now and ask deployments to solve target gating through channel plugins or ClawHub integrations.

recommendation.title: Define Core Target Metadata
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core/channel contract for per-message current-agent, other-agent, and ambient target facts, then implement Telegram first with tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the core prompt/history and mention-policy surfaces that would define the shared contract.
